title: indias current account widens marginally april june rbi data shows 2026 09 01
text:
MUMBAI, Sept 1 (Reuters) - India's current account deficit (INCURA=ECI)
, opens new tab
 widened marginally in the April-to-June quarter from a year ago ​on the back of higher commodity prices and a ‌wider trade gap, the country's central bank said on Tuesday.
The gap stood at $4.2 billion, or 0.5% of GDP (INCAPA=ECI)
, opens new tab
, in the first quarter of the ​fiscal year 2026-27, compared with a revised deficit of $3.4 ​billion, or 0.4% of GDP, a year earlier, the Reserve ⁠Bank of India data showed.
In the preceding quarter, the current ​account had recorded a surplus of $6.5 billion.
The current account deficit is ​expected to widen in the second and third quarter of the year, with full-year gap expected at close 0.9% of GDP, Aditi Nayar, chief economist ​at ICRA, said.
"This would be comfortably financed, aided by the ​sizeable foreign currency non-resident deposit inflows, which should lead to an accretion to ‌reserves ⁠in 2026-27 after a gap of two years," she said.
India's merchandise trade deficit (INTRDQ=ECI)
, opens new tab
 widened to $86.1 billion from $68.9 billion a year earlier, the RBI said.
The country's balance of payments (INBOP=ECI)
, opens new tab
 recorded a deficit of $8.1 ​billion, compared with ​a surplus ⁠of $4.5 billion a year earlier.
Private transfer receipts, which are mainly remittances by Indians employed overseas, increased ​to $42.9 billion in the quarter, from an upwardly revised $33.2 ​billion ⁠a year earlier.
The RBI had in June opened special schemes allowing banks to raise foreign currency deposits and bonds, incentivising them by ⁠offering a ​discount on the dollar-rupee swap rate.
Economists ​expect the schemes to draw more than $80 billion to $90 billion, helping India's balance of ​payments for the year.
(This story has been corrected to say trade deficit widened, not narrowed, in paragraph 4.)
